string.name: study_whiteboard_instructions
string.value: Study → More → Handwriting opens the complete Huawei Pen Kit with its official pen, ballpoint pen, pencil, marker, highlighter, mosaic brush, eraser, lasso, laser, history, shape generation and point prediction. Close, Reset and Transparency stay above the canvas; Show Answer and rating controls stay below it. The canvas uses the complete width of the remaining middle region. Zoom and pan are clipped to that region without covering either set of buttons. Two fingers zoom and pan the card and ink together between scales 1 and 4. Pinching can shrink back to scale 1 but never below it; Reset also returns to scale 1. Until a real pen down is detected in this opening, one finger stays with the writing engine and two fingers pan/zoom. Huawei requires native finger writing to be enabled for finger ink. The first SourceTool.Pen down latches pen mode even after the pen lifts: when zoomed, one finger pans the shared view, two fingers still pan/zoom, and the pen uses the original brushes. Pen contact blocks palm navigation. Closing clears detection; reopening starts undetected. Reset, next card and temporary input disabling retain the mode. Once pen mode is latched, fingers cannot draw or erase in the drawing area at scale 1 or when zoomed. Scale 1 has no single-finger panning. The fallback follows its brush, eraser and stylus-only settings; finger input in the drawing area after detection cannot draw or erase. Pressure, brush type and connection state are not used to guess pen input; unknown input cannot enable the mode. Hit testing records a real pen down first. In pen mode, drawing-area finger input belongs exclusively to the shared viewport from Down, so stationary taps cannot leave ink dots. Pen input and undetected finger writing retain default delivery. Native tools are allowed using public FrameNode click bindings, Slider types and current transformed bounds, without private IDs or changes to SDK controls. Actual HSP tool structure needs device acceptance. A new finger down reconciles active pointers if the child consumed pen up. Huawei brushes and its existing finger-writing disable switch remain; the switch has no app read/control integration. App pen mode comes from actual pen contact. Successful navigation cancels current drawing touches first; sliders retain input and SDK recognizers are not persistently disabled. Drawing fingers intercepted from Down can navigate without child cancellation; other navigation is rejected when cancellation is unavailable. HSP delivery, cancelled ink and palm isolation need device acceptance. Only current study content changes, not other pages or the system screen. The internal Huawei pen toolbar still moves and scales with the complete component; it has not been fixed beside Show Answer. The fallback toolbar is fixed. Reset restores only the app view to scale 1 and its initial position, preserving ink, card and controller; it does not reset Huawei internal vertical scrolling. API 23 and later disable SDK zoom but retain the long canvas and native vertical scrolling, without per-frame scrollTo compensation. Earlier systems need device acceptance. Paper defaults to 80% transparency, saved locally after manual changes and restored on reopening or restart. 100% is transparent; 0% covers the card. Ink and tools do not fade. Save failures are shown; paper_transparency_saved=false cannot mean remembered. Back or Escape dismisses the opacity popup before hiding handwriting. Closing preserves ink and view while the ordinary card returns to its original size; reopening restores the view. The next card clears ink and resets the view; leaving study releases it. Close handwriting for multiple-choice actions. Only capability, context, load, initialization or timeout failures select local Canvas. engine identifies huawei_pen_kit or local_canvas; ready confirms initialization and host layout, not device acceptance. navigation_scope=study_content and navigation=global_pan_zoom identify shared view navigation; view_scale/view_x/view_y report the real view. pen_detected reports whether a real pen down was received in this opening, not connection state or the Huawei switch. Both engines report single_finger_navigation=viewport_pan after detection when zoomed; latched mode at scale 1 reports blocked. Before pen detection, Huawei reports native_input and the fallback brush, subject to its real stylus_only setting. There is no separate ink_offset_x, and Huawei internal vertical position has no read integration. toolbar_follows_view=true states the official toolbar limitation; official scale separately reports SDK scale. paper_transparency/paper_transparency_saved/opacity_open report transparency, confirmed persistence and popup state. No delegated JIDE tools were added. Official brush selection, color, width, internal popups and history have no JIDE read or delegated control integration; transparency has no assistant write tool. Neither engine recognizes handwriting, so JIDE cannot read or grade ink.

Checks cards, notes and study history, attempts repairs and optimizes the database. Repairs can change or delete invalid data, so back up first.

Severe damage may need an existing backup restored under Data management → Backups.

Audio and images are shared by the collection. After deletion, if unused media from this deck can be cleaned up, the app asks separately whether to move it to the media trash. You can also check and manage unused files in Settings > Data Management > Media Management.

Optimize parameters and compare estimated study time in Deck settings. Save to apply the results.

string.name: deck_learn_steps_help
string.value:
Separate waits with spaces: 1m 10m means 1 minute and 10 minutes; enter 30s for 30 seconds. Units: s seconds, m minutes, h hours, d days. No unit means minutes.

Again returns to the first step, Good advances and Easy skips remaining steps. Hard usually averages the first two waits on the first step and repeats the current step later.

After learning, SM-2 uses the first-review setting and FSRS calculates the interval. Blank steps let FSRS choose intervals; keep manual steps within one study day.

string.value: Enter positive waits separated by spaces, such as 10m, or leave blank.

string.name: deck_newPerDay_help
string.value:
The maximum new cards to study each day. Unused capacity does not carry over.

The review limit also applies by default: with a limit of 200 and 190 reviews assigned, at most 10 new cards fit. New cards ignore review limit changes this rule. Parent-deck limits and sibling-card burying can also reduce the count.

string.name: deck_reviewsPerDay_help
string.value:
The maximum due review cards assigned each day, including interday learning cards. Same-day learning cards are not limited by this value.

Excess cards keep their due dates and may become overdue. By default, using the review limit also stops new cards.

string.name: deck_learnSteps_help
string.value:
Wait times for learning steps, separated by spaces. For example, 1m 10m means 1 minute and 10 minutes. Units: s seconds, m minutes, h hours, d days. No unit means minutes.

When blank, SM-2 skips the steps and FSRS chooses short-term intervals.

string.name: deck_relearnSteps_help
string.value:
Wait times after Again, separated by spaces. For example, 10m means study again in 10 minutes. Units: s seconds, m minutes, h hours, d days. No unit means minutes.

When blank, SM-2 skips relearning steps and FSRS chooses short-term intervals.

string.name: deck_newPerDayMinimum_help
string.value: A reserved field for older configurations. It currently has no scheduling effect and can be left unchanged.

string.name: deck_graduatingIntervalGood_help
string.value:
Days until the first review after a new card completes its last learning step with Good. For example, 1 normally makes it due on the next study day.

SM-2 only; FSRS calculates this interval.

string.name: deck_graduatingIntervalEasy_help
string.value:
Easy skips remaining learning steps and schedules the first review after this many days. For example, 4 normally means about 4 days later.

An interval at least as long as Good is recommended. SM-2 only; FSRS calculates this interval.

string.name: deck_newCardInsertOrder_help
string.value:
Controls the initial position (due number) new cards get; lower numbers are learned first. Existing new cards are repositioned when you change this.
“Due order”: first added, first learned. “Random”: new cards get random positions.
Official advice: with the v3 scheduler, keep “Due order” and control draw order via “New card gather order” instead.

string.name: deck_newCardGatherPriority_help
string.value:
Chooses which new cards to gather before reaching the daily limit:
Deck order: subdeck names, then card positions.
Deck, then random notes: subdeck names, then random notes within each.
Lowest/highest position: smallest/largest position first.
Random notes: random notes, then their cards.
Random cards: random cards.

Limits and sibling skipping still apply. Deck-name order does not follow home-screen dragging; New card display order controls presentation afterward.

string.name: deck_newCardSortOrder_help
string.value:
Sets the order of gathered new cards:
Card template, then gathering order: group by template and keep order within each.
Gathering order: keep the original order; sibling cards are often adjacent.
Card template, then random: group by template and shuffle within each.
Random note, then template: shuffle notes and show each note’s cards in template order.
Random cards: shuffle all cards.

To separate forward and reverse cards, choose Card template, then gathering order.

string.name: deck_newMix_help
string.value:
When new cards appear relative to reviews: mixed with reviews / after reviews / before reviews.
Example: “After reviews” clears today's due reviews before any new cards; “Before reviews” teaches new cards first.

string.name: deck_interdayLearningMix_help
string.value:
Places interday learning cards mixed with, before or after review cards.
Interday learning cards enter the day-based queue when a step crosses the study-day boundary; the delay need not be a full 24 hours. This does not order intraday learning cards waiting for a short delay.

string.name: deck_minimumLapseInterval_help
string.value:
SM-2 only: the minimum review interval after a lapse, normally 1 day, also constrained by the maximum review interval. It does not set fixed relearning-step delays or guarantee a 1-day interval after every lapse.
FSRS does not use this minimum.

string.name: deck_leechThreshold_help
string.value:
After a review card is answered Again this many times in total, it is marked as a leech.
Example: 8 means the card becomes a leech on its 8th lapse.
Leeches consume a lot of time. Official advice: rewrite the card, delete it, or devise a mnemonic for it.

string.name: deck_leechAction_help
string.value:
When the leech threshold is reached:

• Tag only: add leech to the note and keep scheduling the card.
• Suspend card: add the tag and suspend the current card until manually restored.

Search for tag:leech in Browse to find and improve these notes.

string.name: deck_reviewOrder_help
string.value:
Orders gathered review cards: ascending due date shows earlier due cards first; ascending/descending interval shows shorter/longer intervals first.

Lower ease usually means harder cards. Ascending retrievability shows cards more likely to be forgotten first; descending shows those more likely to be recalled first. Random shuffles cards.

Does not change daily limits or due dates.

string.name: deck_buryNew_help
string.value: After studying a new card, skip other new cards from the same note today to avoid giving away answers. They return next study day, subject to deck limits.

string.name: deck_buryReviews_help
string.value: After studying a review card, skip other review cards from the same note today to avoid giving away answers. They return next study day, subject to due dates and deck limits.

string.name: deck_buryInterdayLearning_label
string.value: Skip sibling interday learning cards today

string.name: deck_buryInterdayLearning_help
string.value:
Skip eligible interday learning cards from the same note today to avoid giving away answers.

Interday means crossing the study-day boundary, without necessarily waiting 24 hours. Same-day learning cards are unaffected.

string.name: deck_disableAutoplay_help
string.value:
When on, card audio no longer plays automatically; tap the play button manually.
Example: enable it in libraries or at night so flipping a card never makes sudden noise.

string.name: deck_skipQuestionWhenReplayingAnswer_help
string.value:
When replaying answer audio, the question part of the audio is skipped.
Example: a card has “question recording + answer recording”; replaying the answer plays only the answer part.

string.name: deck_waitForAudio_help
string.value:
For regular flashcard Auto Advance, wait for audio to finish before actions such as showing the answer, rating or reminding. The configured delay must also have elapsed.
Choice cards use their own grading-feedback and continuation flow, independent of this option.

string.name: deck_capAnswerTimeToSecs_help
string.value: Maximum answer time for statistics: 1–7200 seconds. Time beyond the limit is excluded; it does not automatically reveal or rate the card.

string.name: deck_showTimer_help
string.value:
Shows the time spent on the current card on the study page.
Example: enable it to pace yourself, e.g. answering within 15 seconds per card.

string.name: deck_stopTimerOnAnswer_help
string.value: Freeze the on-screen timer when the answer is shown. Study statistics still include time until you grade the answer.

string.name: deck_secondsToShowQuestion_help
string.value:
For regular flashcards, wait this long on the question side before the question action. 0 disables it. Study > More > Auto advance lets you adjust durations and actions, then start or pause, for this session only.
Choice cards do not use this timer.

string.name: deck_secondsToShowAnswer_help
string.value:
For regular flashcards, wait this long on the answer side before the answer action. 0 disables it. Study > More > Auto advance lets you adjust durations and actions, then start or pause, for this session only.
Choice cards use a separate feedback duration.

string.name: deck_questionAction_help
string.value: For regular flashcards, show the answer or a reminder when the question timer expires. A reminder does not flip the card. Auto Advance must be started first. Choice cards do not use this action.

string.name: deck_answerAction_help
string.value:
For regular flashcards, skip today, rate Again / Good / Hard, or show a reminder when the answer timer expires. Auto Advance must be started first.
Choice cards rate automatically from the grading result instead of using this action.

string.name: deck_desiredRetention_help
string.value:
The target chance of remembering a card when due, from 70% to 99%. For example, 90% schedules a review at a predicted nine-in-ten chance of recall.

Higher targets usually need more reviews. This is a target, not a measured correct-answer rate.

string.name: deck_fsrsParams4_help
string.value: FSRS 4 parameters, normally calculated by optimization. The first nonempty set is used in v6, v5, v4 order; all empty uses defaults. Save optimized results to apply them to decks sharing the preset.

string.name: deck_easyDaysPercentages_help
string.value:
Enter seven values from 0 to 1, Monday through Sunday: 1 is normal, 0.5 requests fewer reviews and 0 requests as few as possible.

Values are not exact percentages and cannot guarantee a review-free day. Cards move only within their allowed due-date range.

string.name: deck_fsrsParams5_help
string.value: FSRS 5 parameters, normally calculated by optimization. The first nonempty set is used in v6, v5, v4 order; all empty uses defaults. Save optimized results to apply them to decks sharing the preset.

string.name: deck_fsrsParams6_help
string.value: FSRS 6 parameters, normally calculated by optimization. The first nonempty set is used in v6, v5, v4 order; all empty uses defaults. Save optimized results to apply them to decks sharing the preset.

string.name: deck_historicalRetention_help
string.value: Estimated past retention when early study history is missing. Accepts 50%–100%.

string.name: deck_paramSearch_help
string.value:
An Anki search query selecting cards for FSRS parameter optimization. When empty, optimization uses non-suspended cards in the current preset; otherwise it uses the specified query.

The query is used when you select Optimize. Editing it does not start training or change the Browse query.

string.name: deck_initialEase_help
string.value: Initial ease after a new card finishes learning, affecting later SM-2 review intervals. Higher values usually mean longer waits. Accepts 1.31–5.

string.name: deck_easyMultiplier_help
string.value: Used to calculate the interval after Easy. Higher values usually mean longer waits. SM-2 only; accepts 1–5.

string.name: deck_hardMultiplier_help
string.value: Used to calculate the interval after Hard. Higher values usually mean longer waits. SM-2 only; accepts 0.5–1.3.

string.name: deck_lapseMultiplier_help
string.value: After Again, multiply the previous interval by this value. Zero starts from the minimum review interval without turning the card into a new card. SM-2 only; accepts 0–1.

string.name: deck_intervalMultiplier_help
string.value: Adjusts SM-2 review intervals: 1 is normal; higher usually means later reviews and lower earlier reviews. Does not change learning steps. Accepts 0.5–2.

string.name: deck_maximumReviewInterval_help
string.value:
The upper limit in days when calculating review intervals, normally 36500 days.
For example, 365 caps newly calculated review intervals at 365 days. Whether a card is actually shown on its due date also depends on studying, daily limits and states such as suspension.

string.name: deck_ignoreRevlogsBeforeDate_help
string.value:
Enter YYYY-MM-DD to ignore earlier records when FSRS optimizes parameters or calculates memory states. Blank means no cutoff. History and statistics remain.

Also affects missing-state initialization and later recalculation. Changing only the date does not guarantee immediate recalculation of all cards. Optimization uses the current draft date when started.

string.name: add_note_deck_help
string.value: Choose the deck for these new cards, defaulting to the deck you were viewing. Changing decks does not change their content.

string.name: add_note_notetype_help
string.value: Choose how you want to study: question and answer, cloze deletions in a sentence, or masks on an image. Switching types asks before discarding a draft.

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_help
string.value:
Fill in the question on the front and the answer on the back to create one card.

Study the question, then reveal the answer.

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_reversed_help
string.value:
Fill in the front and back to create two cards, one in each direction.

For vocabulary, one card asks for the translation and the other asks for the original word.

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_optional_reversed_help
string.value:
Fill in the front and back, then choose whether to enable “Also create a reverse card”.

Off creates one front-to-back card. On adds a back-to-front card. Both cards share the same content.

string.name: add_note_notetype_cloze_help
string.value:
Enter a sentence, select text and use the cloze buttons.

New cloze uses a new number; each number creates one card. Same cloze uses the largest current number so those parts hide together, or c1 when no number exists. Extra back content is optional.

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_type_answer_help
string.value:
Enter a question on the front and its correct answer on the back. This creates one card that asks you to type the answer.

Reveal the answer to compare your input, then grade your recall.

string.name: add_note_notetype_image_occlusion_help
string.value:
Choose an image and open the mask editor. Draw rectangles over the areas you want to recall.

Masks sharing a number are studied together; different numbers create separate cards. The title and extra answer information are optional. Reopen the editor to adjust confirmed masks.

string.name: add_note_tags_help
string.value: Tags filter notes across decks. Separate tags with spaces and hierarchy levels with ::. For example, English CET4::Listening is two tags. Leave blank for none.

string.value: The cloze format is invalid. Check markers such as c1 and c2.

string.value: Delete tags not associated with any notes

string.value: Remove all tags not associated with any notes?

string.name: deck_reviewLimit_help
string.value:
A daily review limit that applies only to this deck, overriding the preset; leave blank to follow the preset.
Example: with a preset of 200 reviews/day, entering 50 for the “Medicine” deck caps Medicine at 50 reviews a day, while decks using the preset are unaffected.

string.name: deck_newLimit_help
string.value:
A daily new-card limit that applies only to this deck, overriding the preset; leave blank to follow the preset.
Example: with a preset of 20 new cards/day, entering 5 for the “Speaking” deck introduces at most 5 new cards there each day.

string.name: deck_reviewToday_help
string.value:
A review limit for the current study day. Enter a value, turn on the corresponding switch and save; 0 gives no allowance for that category today.
Saving with an empty value or the switch off clears the override. It expires at the next study day, falling back to this deck’s limit, then the preset if no deck limit is set. Study days may not change at midnight.

string.name: deck_newToday_help
string.value:
A new-card limit for the current study day. Enter a value, turn on the corresponding switch and save; 0 gives no allowance for that category today.
Saving with an empty value or the switch off clears the override. It expires at the next study day, falling back to this deck’s limit, then the preset if no deck limit is set. Study days may not change at midnight.

string.name: deck_reviewTodayActive_help
string.value:
Turn on and save to apply today’s review limit. Turning it off keeps the number in the open form, but saving clears the override rather than storing a disabled temporary value.
After disabling or expiry, this deck’s limit applies first, with the preset used only when there is no deck override.

string.name: deck_newTodayActive_help
string.value:
Turn on and save to apply today’s new-card limit. Turning it off keeps the number in the open form, but saving clears the override rather than storing a disabled temporary value.
After disabling or expiry, this deck’s limit applies first, with the preset used only when there is no deck override.

string.name: deck_desiredRetentionOverride_help
string.value:
Applies only to this deck. Leave blank to use the preset.

For a 90% preset, entering 95 usually schedules more frequent reviews for this deck; others keep 90%.

string.name: deck_newCardsIgnoreReviewLimit_help
string.value:
By default, new cards stop appearing once the review limit is exhausted; when on, new cards appear regardless of the review limit.
Example: the 200-card review limit is fully consumed by reviews — with this on, new cards still appear today (making the day's total load heavier). This is a collection-wide setting affecting all decks.

string.name: deck_fsrsEnabled_help
string.value:
Schedule reviews from answer history for all decks. Turning this off uses SM-2. Other synced clients must support FSRS.

Optimize current preset uses its study history, excluding suspended cards by default. Optimize all presets calculates each preset separately. Save to apply the results to decks using those presets.

You can also compare estimated study time at different desired retentions.

string.name: deck_applyAllParentLimits_help
string.value:
By default, studying from a child deck ignores the daily limits of decks above it; when on, limits apply level by level starting from the topmost deck.
Example: “Languages” (limit 50) contains “English” (limit 30); with this on, studying from English is also bounded by Languages' 50 — both levels constrain at once. Useful for capping an entire deck tree. This is a collection-wide setting.

string.name: deck_fsrsReschedule_help
string.value:
When on, saving recalculates affected due dates. When off, current due dates remain and future answers use the new settings.

Applies to the selected deck scope. The global FSRS switch affects all decks. Many cards may take time.

string.name: deck_fsrsHealthCheck_help
string.value: During optimization, checks how parameters fit study history. Limited history may prevent evaluation. Saving the switch alone does not run checks or repair the database.

string.name: deck_range_validation_error
string.value: This value is outside Anki's allowed range.

string.name: deck_fsrs_parameters_validation_error
string.value: The number of FSRS parameters is invalid.

string.name: deck_easy_days_validation_error
string.value: Easy Days requires seven numbers or an empty value.

string.name: today_empty_no_decks_hint
string.value: Tap New beside the summary to create a deck

string.name: ankiweb_guide_message
string.value: JideCards is a local-first, open-source flashcard app with no preloaded study content. You can download community-shared decks from AnkiWeb and import them. Online sync and AI features use the services you configure and choose to access.

string.name: ankiweb_guide_notice
string.value: Please review the deck source, content quality, and usage license.

string.name: glossary_bury_help
string.value:
Skip this card today without deleting it. It returns on the next study day, which starts at the configured hour rather than necessarily at midnight.

To restore it early, choose Restore buried cards on the completion page, or select buried cards in the browser and choose Bury / Unbury.

Use this for a one-day break. Rate Again when you cannot recall the answer. Use Suspend for a longer break.

string.name: glossary_suspend_help
string.value:
Stops this card until you restore it manually. Content, due date and study history remain.

Select suspended cards in the browser and choose Suspend / Unsuspend to restore them. Use Bury for a one-day break. Suspending a buried card stops its automatic return.

string.name: glossary_delete_help
string.value:
Deletes the current card, keeping other cards from the same note. Deleting the last card also deletes its note.

Undo the current undoable action under the review page’s More → Undo. Syncing or closing the collection may clear undo history.

string.name: glossary_undo_help
string.value:
Undo the last available action, such as a rating, skipping, suspension or deletion.

In study, choose More → Undo. On home or in the browser, choose More → Revert. Syncing or closing the collection may clear history.

string.name: glossary_ratings_help
string.value:
For regular flashcards, recall the answer, show it, then rate your recall.

Again: You forgot or answered incorrectly.
Hard: You answered correctly with difficulty.
Good: You recalled the answer normally.
Easy: You answered correctly without effort.

The time below each button estimates when this card will be reviewed again if you choose that rating. Rate your recall, rather than the delay you prefer.

Choice cards use a separate flow: select and submit, then the app automatically rates a correct answer Good and an incorrect answer Hard. The regular four rating buttons are not shown. These automatic ratings also enter review statistics.

string.name: glossary_leech_help
string.value:
A review card becomes a leech after enough Again ratings, 8 by default.

Deck settings can add the leech tag alone or also suspend the card. Search tag:leech in the browser to find and improve difficult content.

string.name: glossary_siblings_help
string.value:
Several cards generated from one note, such as forward and reverse cards or different cloze numbers.

Deck settings can bury sibling cards for today to avoid giving away answers. Interday learning crosses the study-day boundary without necessarily waiting 24 hours. Same-day minute-based learning cards are not automatically buried by these rules.

string.name: glossary_graduating_interval_help
string.value:
How long a new card waits for its first review after learning.

Good on the last step waits 1 day by default. Easy skips remaining steps and waits 4 days. Change these values in Deck settings.

SM-2 only; FSRS calculates the interval.

string.name: glossary_fsrs_retention_help
string.value:
The target chance of remembering a card when it is due, 90% by default. Raising it usually increases reviews; lowering it usually increases forgetting.

This is an algorithm target, not the measured pass rate or a guarantee. Set it for the preset or current deck in Deck settings.

string.name: glossary_fuzz_label
string.value: Small random changes to review dates

string.name: glossary_fuzz_help
string.value:
The app moves reviews slightly earlier or later within allowed limits to avoid many cards becoming due together.

Same-day learning can add up to 25% to the wait, capped at 5 minutes. Buttons do not show this extra delay. This feature cannot currently be disabled.

string.name: glossary_shortcuts_help
string.value:
Default jidecards study keyboard shortcuts (regular flashcards):

• Space / Enter: show the answer on the question side; rate Good on the answer side.
• 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 (including the number pad): rate Again / Hard / Good / Easy on the answer side.
• E: edit note; * (usually Shift+8): toggle mark.
• Ctrl+1–7 (including the number pad): toggle flags.
• - / B: skip today.
• @ (usually Shift+2) / S: suspend the card.
• Delete: delete the current card with confirmation.
• Ctrl+Z: undo the available action.
• Esc: go back.

string.value:
Replaces text in note fields, affecting every card from those notes.

Find cannot be blank. A blank replacement deletes matched text. Leave the field name blank for all fields or enter its actual name for one field. Regex replacements can use $1 and $2 for captured text.

Selected notes uses the current selection. Current search results uses the full results, including unloaded rows. Changing the search afterward does not change the submitted scope.

string.name: browser_help_batch_body
string.value:
Hold a row to select multiple items, then open Selected X. Note mode processes every card from the selected notes.

Move or mark: keeps study progress. Stars belong to notes; flags belong to cards.
Suspend / Unsuspend: restores all cards when all are suspended; otherwise suspends them all.
Bury / Unbury: restores all when all are buried; otherwise buries them all. Suspended cards remain suspended. Buried cards return next study day; suspended cards need manual restoration. Restoring keeps due dates and study progress without guaranteeing immediate study.
Delete: card mode deletes selected cards and notes left without cards. Note mode deletes whole notes and their cards.

Set due date (card mode): enter 60 or 60-90 to assign days or a random date in that range. New cards become review cards. FSRS memory states cause intervals to be recalculated; without them, intervals normally remain and ! forces a new interval.
Reposition (card mode): new cards only. Positions follow note order, start and step; sibling cards share positions. Random shuffles notes; Shift existing moves new cards from the insertion point onward.
Change note type: check field and template mappings. Unmapped content or old cards may be deleted, and new templates may create cards. Full sync is required afterward; downloading overwrites local edits.

Undo deletion and other actions under More → Revert; sync or closing the collection may clear history.

string.name: browser_find_regex_help
string.value:
When enabled, Find matches a regular expression against field text. • Character classes: [a-z], \d, \w, \s • Repetition: *, +, ?, {n,m} • ^ and $ match the start and end of the entire field by default. Add (?m) for line-by-line matching. HTML
is not a newline character. • Capture groups: use () and reference them with $1, $2, etc. in the replacement; use $$ for a literal dollar sign. • Escape special characters such as ., * and ( with a preceding backslash. Examples: \d+ matches digits; (?m)^hello.* matches text lines starting with hello; replace (\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2}) with $3/$2/$1 to reformat dates.

string.name: stats_help_today
string.value:
Studied today counts answers, including repeated answers to one card. Due reviews includes overdue cards, excludes new cards and is not capped by daily limits.

Time comes from answer records. Mature cards had an interval of at least 21 days before answering. Hard, Good and Easy count as passes; incorrect choice answers receive Hard, so this is not choice-question accuracy.

string.name: stats_help_forecast
string.value:
Counts future reviews from current due dates, without predicting scheduling changes from future answers. Excludes new and suspended cards and is not capped by daily limits.

Bar height is the card count for a day or combined date range. Backlog includes overdue cards.

Daily load estimates the long-term average by summing 1/interval in days, treating intervals below one day as one day.

string.name: stats_help_card_counts
string.value:
Shows card counts and percentages by state. Young and mature reviews are separated at a 21-day interval.

Separating suspended and buried cards counts them on their own; otherwise they remain in their original card type. Buried cards return on the next study day.

string.name: stats_help_hours
string.value:
Counts answers by hour from 0 to 23, including repeated answers to one card. Taller bars mean more answers.

Excludes early filtered-deck reviews, manual due-date changes and rescheduling records.

string.name: stats_help_ease
string.value:
Bar height shows cards in each range.

SM-2 shows ease: higher usually means easier. FSRS shows difficulty: higher means harder. Values from the two algorithms are not directly comparable.

string.name: stats_help_interval
string.value:
Shows current review intervals: days on the horizontal axis and card counts as bar height. The median appears below.

Range sets the horizontal limit: 1 month means up to 30 days; 50% and 95% show intervals through those card-count percentiles; All shows the full range. It does not filter past study history.

string.name: stats_help_stability
string.value:
FSRS only. Stability estimates the days for recall probability to fall from 100% to 90%; longer usually means less likely to forget.

The horizontal axis is days and bar height is card count. This measures memory strength, not the scheduled review interval.

string.name: stats_help_retention
string.value:
Pass rate for eligible answer records: Hard, Good and Easy pass; Again fails. Every answer is counted separately.

Young and mature cards are separated by whether the previous interval reached 21 days. Counts review ratings that affect scheduling; other learning and relearning records require a prior interval of at least 1 day. Manual due-date changes and previews that do not reschedule are excluded.

This is not FSRS desired retention or choice-question accuracy. Longer periods are more informative.

string.name: stats_help_retrievability
string.value:
FSRS estimates the chance of recalling cards today; this is not a test result. Bar height shows cards in each probability range.

Average recall includes only cards with memory states. Estimated learned cards sums probabilities. Estimated learned notes averages each note’s card probabilities before summing; cards without memory states contribute zero.

Tap a date for its count or arrows to change year. Swipe horizontally on narrow screens. Tap weekday labels to change the week’s starting day. Data follows the selected statistics range.

string.name: stats_help_reviews
string.value:
Shows answer counts by date. Time switches to answer duration. Each bar covers one day or several combined days; colors separate learning, relearning and review stages.

string.value:

string.value: What can flashcards help you learn?

string.name: home_intro_flashcards_body
string.value:
Flashcards put a question on the front and an answer on the back. Recall first, then reveal the answer. JideCards schedules spaced reviews based on your recall.

Practice vocabulary, languages, medicine, law, coursework, exams, history, or skills for work. Keep each card focused on one point.

string.value: No need to explore complex settings first

string.name: home_intro_simple_start_body
string.value: Import an existing deck, or create a deck and add cards, to start studying. Begin with the defaults, then adjust appearance, reminders, or deck settings as you become familiar with the review routine.

string.name: home_intro_apkg_title
string.value: Import an APKG and start learning

string.name: home_intro_apkg_body
string.value:
An APKG (.apkg) is an Anki deck package that can include images and audio. Choose New deck → Import file on the home screen, select a file, and confirm the import options. CSV / TSV / TXT files support preview and field mapping.

Recall → Show answer → Rate your recall: Again, Hard, Good, or Easy. The times below the buttons are estimated review intervals. Complete your due reviews each day.

string.name: home_intro_agent_title
string.value: Create and edit cards with an Agent

string.name: home_intro_agent_body
string.value:
Try an Agent such as WorkBuddy or TRAE that can work with files and run code. Provide your notes or study materials, specify the scope, card count, and format, and ask for an importable .apkg file.

Create: “Make 20 question-and-answer cards from this material. Ask one point per card, keep answers short, and generate an APKG with the required media.”

Edit: export an APKG from More in the deck details, then ask: “Add explanations, shorten answers, and correct errors. Preserve note identifiers and media, and output an updated APKG.” Keep the original as a backup and check the result before importing. Changing identifiers or note types may create duplicates.

string.name: home_actions_instructions
string.value: Six icon-only buttons always form one row above the home summary. More stands alone in the upper-left corner. JIDE, Search, Browse, Sync and New form a right-aligned group in that order, with New at the far right and flexible space between the two groups. Phones and split layouts use the same arrangement. Buttons use the same 44vp footprint, page margins and toolbar position as the shared Back and More controls. The gap before the summary follows the shared page density. Widths, gaps and glyphs shrink together in very narrow windows without wrapping. The top buttons, summary and More/New popups share the card corner radius. The summary fills the width below. More and New reuse the public menu popup without arrows, aligned to the left and right ends below the button row. Long menus scroll internally, close on outside clicks, and avoid system bars, camera cutouts and the navigation indicator. Sync and Browse open directly from Home; sync status appears on the Sync button: a red exclamation means not logged in or a full upload/download is required, and a dot means pending changes. Transfers show a spinner; conflicts and failures keep an exclamation and open the current task details. JIDE appears only when enabled for the channel. Home does not use holding-hand detection.

string.name: home_search_instructions
string.value: Typing a name, full path or local alias filters decks, including collapsed children and excluding hidden subtrees. Selecting a result opens its existing details. Filtering does not change home expansion. Selecting a deck uses the existing ancestor expansion and details behavior without modifying deck data or study order.

string.name: note_editor_wheel_instructions
string.value: The semicircle opens by default and reflects current formats, without executing a tool or opening a popup. Each circular button contains an icon above its name, with long names on two lines. The inner arc holds Bold, Italic, Underline, Highlight, Line break and Clear formatting. Both Simple and Experimental modes show the rotating outer arc with up to seven link, math, font size, heading, script, list or cloze tools. Cloze tools appear only in fields that support cloze. In Visual editing, Bold, Italic, Underline and Highlight can be active together; click one again to disable it. Lists, line breaks, math, scripts, links, clear formatting, cloze and Source-format insertions only flash briefly after clicking. Font size and Heading share a local arc outside the wheel, aligned with the direction of their trigger button and adjusted along the wheel to avoid screen and keyboard edges, without resizing the wheel. The current size or heading option is highlighted; a button with an applied format stays highlighted after the options close. Mixed selections have no selected option. Tap the trigger again to close. Visual editing displays sizes and headings directly: sizes apply to selected text or later typing, and headings apply to whole paragraphs. Source editing writes HTML. Fixed options have no track through the buttons. Tap Math for inline delimiters; hold for display or chemistry options without also inserting inline delimiters. Dragging or mouse scrolling preserves active formats and never applies a centered tool. Two mouse notches move one item. Collapsing preserves formats; reopening resets the format selection without changing existing content. The menu targets the first editable field until another is focused and remains when the keyboard closes. Each editor has Visual and Source editing buttons above it, and a state-changing Expand or Collapse icon at its bottom right. Closing first-use help continues the clicked action. The handle arrow turns with the menu; drag vertically to move, hold to switch sides, or use supported holding-hand awareness.

string.name: browser_preferences_instructions
string.value: Cards or notes, status and sort share one row below search. All three use a selection dialog: confirm with the top-right check button or close to discard the draft. Sort fields appear once with separate direction controls. The filter button opens the deck, tag and saved-search sidebar; deck and tag searches use the same tree input. Clicking a row opens preview first: Cards previews current search results, while Notes previews all cards of the current note. Edit from the preview. The More menu selects all results, configures display columns, and opens search options or shortcut help. Cards and notes save separate column lists. Mode, sort, subtitle and recent searches persist. Wide windows support explicitly opening an editor beside the list. Selection actions include preview, export, grade now and maintenance; deletion and grading require confirmation. Select all includes unloaded rows. Ctrl+A inside inputs and editors selects text.

string.name: note_drawing_instructions
string.value: In Images and videos, New whiteboard drawing appears below Add image or video. The pen icon at the top right of an image opens the same drawing editor; videos have no image editor. Drawing uses the existing complete Huawei handwriting suite, with the original ink model as fallback. Existing Huawei ink cannot silently change engines. Choose text color in the shared selector. Tap text to show a selection box fitted to its glyphs, then edit, drag or delete it. Drag any of the four edge or four corner handles in any direction, or pinch, to resize text proportionally; there is no font-size selector. Tap empty space to deselect. Use Add image on a blank canvas or Replace image when an image is present. Replacing the image keeps ink and text. You can also choose a blank canvas size. Done produces a regular PNG with embedded editable source; Cancel preserves the original. Media Done only transfers the field draft; saving the note uses existing media sync and export. Observations expose engine, text count, selection and transformation states, color options and tool availability, never background, ink, text contents or paths. They do not authorize assistant drawing, image reading or automatic importing. Huawei internal tools and direct dragging and resizing are not fully observed.

string.name: note_visual_instructions
string.value: When adding or editing a note, click the existing image icon beside a field title to manage images and videos. Add image or video opens the system picker; New whiteboard drawing appears below it. The pen icon at the top right of an image opens handwriting and text editing and creates a new image. Videos support preview, replacement and removal. Supported videos: MP4, MOV and WebM, up to 64 MiB each; playback depends on device codec support. Done applies to the field draft; Cancel discards dialog changes. Saving the note writes media and uses existing media sync and export. Image occlusion source selection only accepts images. Observations provide attachment types, counts, busy state and available actions; they do not read video contents or enable automatic picking or playback.
